iterations.prompt:
You are analyzing a mathematical paper written in LaTeX. Extract ALL mathematical definitions.

Definition forms:
1. \begin{definition}...\end{definition}
2. "Definition 2.1. ..."
3. "We define X as/to be ...", "X is defined as ...", "Let X be ..."
4. Implicit definitions with new notation

For each definition, extract:
- name: Short descriptive name
- raw_latex: Original LaTeX text (preserve ALL math notation)
- clean_text: Human-readable version (keep [MATH] for formulas)
- label: Any \label{...} or null

Return JSON array:
[
  {
    "name": "descriptive name",
    "raw_latex": "original LaTeX",
    "clean_text": "readable text",
    "label": "label or null"
  }
]

You are analyzing a mathematical paper written in LaTeX. Extract ALL mathematical definitions.

Definition indicators:
1. Formal environments: \begin{definition}...\end{definition}
2. Numbered definitions: "Definition X.Y. ..."
3. Definitional language: "We define/call X as/to be", "X is defined as", "Let X be", "X is called", "X is said to be"
4. Emphasized new terms: \emph{term} or \textit{term} followed by mathematical description

Extraction requirements:
- Include complete sentences from start of definitional phrase to natural endpoint
- Capture ALL associated mathematical displays (equations, arrays, cases)
- Include surrounding context that clarifies the definition
- Preserve emphasis markers (\emph{}, \textit{}) in output

Exclude:
- Model/algorithm descriptions ("first model", "second approach")
- Isolated formulas without definitional context
- Examples, lemmas, theorems, propositions
- Computational procedures or experimental setups

For each definition, extract:
- name: Short descriptive name based on emphasized or defined term
- raw_latex: Complete original LaTeX text preserving ALL notation and structure
- clean_text: Human-readable version (keep [MATH] for formulas)
- label: Any \label{...} or null
